title: Engine Performance, Emissions and Hybrid Diagnostics
author: Erudior
description: Distinguish fuel delivery, ignition and air-metering faults. Map gasoline and diesel emissions controls, diagnose a trainer and verify its restored function. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added an individual parts atlas, hands-on modification workshop, instance-level build ledger and pre/post verification.

lessons.title: Read fuel control in context
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Automotive Electrical Systems and Diagnosis, Engine and Drivetrain Service, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

The controller estimates fuel from air, speed and load. In closed-loop gasoline operation it adjusts delivery using exhaust feedback. Positive fuel trim means the controller is adding fuel relative to its base estimate. A lean indication can come from extra air, low delivery or biased measurement. A diesel may use EGR, a particulate filter and selective catalytic reduction. Identify the engine and operating strategy before interpreting its data.

## Worked shop case

One gasoline bank shows positive trim at idle that moves toward zero at raised speed. A fixed air leak is relatively more important at idle. Inspect for a leak and test alternatives before replacing an oxygen sensor.

## Guided practice

Short-term trim moves from +15% to +3%. By how many percentage points does it fall?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A scan record, a diagnosed physical trainer and a verified restoration.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Fuel delivery, ignition and air metering
topics: Fuel delivery, ignition and air metering
lessons.body:
In a return-style fuel system, a regulator can send excess fuel from the rail back to the tank. Returnless designs move regulation nearer the tank or vary pump output under control. Port injectors discharge upstream of the intake valve. A gasoline direct-injection system adds a high-pressure stage feeding in-cylinder injectors. A diesel common-rail system stores high-pressure fuel for electronically timed injection. Compare specified pressure at the correct stage and signal under the same load. Use service data and an approved trainer; a high-pressure leak must never be sought by hand.

A mass-airflow sensor reports air mass entering at its location. A speed-density strategy estimates charge from manifold absolute pressure, temperature, speed and calibration. A throttle controls flow on many spark-ignition engines. A distributor routes spark from a shared coil; coil-on-plug dedicates a coil to each plug in a typical design. Compression, fueling and ignition can each cause a cylinder misfire. A misfire code identifies where to investigate.

## Worked shop case

One cylinder repeatedly misfires. On an approved training engine the fault follows an authorized swap of two identical coils, while the injectors and plugs stay put. That supports a coil-related fault. If it stays with the cylinder, use the documented next tests for command, fuel, compression and harness condition before ordering a part.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A direct-injection system's low-side supply tracks command but its high-side rail reading falls under load. Where is evidence missing?
step: Separate the low- and high-pressure stages.
step: Check high-side command, sensor plausibility, pump drive and specified tests.
answer: A good inlet reading alone cannot establish high-side delivery; use model-specific approved diagnostics.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Document an actual donor's pump stages, regulation, air sensors, ignition and diagnostic access. Annotate which data items are measured or estimated and plan a reversible single-variable test on the existing training fixture.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Oxygen feedback, catalysts, EGR, EVAP, DPF and SCR
topics: Oxygen feedback, catalysts, EGR, EVAP, DPF and SCR
lessons.body:
A three-way catalyst in a suitable gasoline system treats hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen near its intended mixture. Upstream feedback sensors help mixture control; a downstream sensor often supports catalyst monitoring. A wideband sensor and a traditional narrowband switching sensor produce different signals. An exhaust leak can bias interpretation. Compare commanded conditions and the service description for the exact sensor before interpreting a graph.

Exhaust gas recirculation dilutes intake charge in selected conditions to reduce peak combustion temperatures and formation of nitrogen oxides. EVAP manages fuel vapors from the tank and purges them under command. A diesel particulate filter retains particulate matter; regeneration oxidizes combustible soot, while ash can accumulate. SCR meters reductant to aid NOx conversion. A differential-pressure sensor and temperature sensors inform different decisions. Keeping required control hardware, calibration and routing intact belongs in the original donor plan and the final as-built review. Use the linked EPA applicability notes.

## Worked shop case

A training diesel reports a high pressure difference across its DPF at a documented flow. A kinked sensing tube, a biased sensor or restriction can affect that observation. Compare key-on/engine-off plausibility, permitted sensor checks and readings at a second specified flow. A forced regeneration is a specialized heat-producing service, and the code by itself does not justify one.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: An unready monitor appears after power was disconnected. What evidence would distinguish incomplete operation from a component failure?
step: Check monitor enable criteria and stored or pending faults.
step: Compare recorded operating conditions with service data.
answer: Report readiness, enabling conditions and actual codes separately; retain the original controls.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Produce an as-designed fuel, vapor and exhaust map for the candidate donor. Mark ports, control devices, catalysts, oxygen or NOx sensors, service access, calibration and evidence of retained function. Add diesel-only devices only where fitted.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Design a scan capture that can separate causes
lessons.body:
Store the complaint, code status, freeze frame, operating mode and units before clearing anything. Choose a signal related to the fault and an independent reference. Define the stimulus, response and stop condition. OBD readiness describes whether a monitor ran. A single unset monitor cannot tell you that its system failed.

## Worked shop case

After an overnight soak a coolant sensor reports 65 °C while ambient and intake air are near 12 °C. Compare the coolant signal with a trusted independent temperature reading and inspect the circuit using its service procedure.

## Guided practice

After a cold soak a trainer reports 40 °C vs an independent 16 °C. Give the magnitude of the discrepancy in °C.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Select a gasoline sensor fault. Compare sensor bias with a wiring fault, name the evidence each predicts, and give a test that separates them. Include a diesel aftertreatment comparison and a model-specific hybrid handoff for an energized-vehicle concern.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Introduce and recover a known sensor fault
lessons.body:
Use a physical training board with documented fault switches or a plug-in simulator attached to a scan tool. Establish a healthy baseline, change one permitted trainer condition, and compare live data and stored information. A real customer vehicle may be used for read-only observation with permission. Do all induced faults on the bench.

## Worked shop case

A trainer's open sensor mode drives its displayed value to an extreme. Returning the switch to normal restores the signal while a history code remains. Record current data and code status separately.

## Guided practice

A trainer reads 18 °C, then 48 °C during a simulated bias. By how many °C did it change?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

Clean Air Act §203(a)(3) addresses tampering and defeat devices. Preserve the designed emissions controls and diagnostic monitoring. A pass in a local inspection or an extinguished fault lamp is insufficient evidence for a modified configuration. Record engine family, original configuration, fault, corrective action and functional checks. Apply the separate federal kit-car policy only to a build that actually fits it.

[EPA — vehicle and engine tampering, Clean Air Act §203(a)(3)](https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/epa-tampering-policy-epa-enforcement-policy-vehicle-and-engine-tampering-and) · [EPA — Kit Car Policy and rebuilt certified configurations](https://www.epa.gov/importing-vehicles-and-engines/kit-car-policy)

## Workshop preparation

Use a protected low-voltage trainer for introduced faults. No emissions-control modification or traction-voltage work. Run a combustion vehicle outdoors only where authorized.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Separate an acoustic improvement from an emissions change
topics: Separate an acoustic improvement from an emissions change
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Engine control, vapor and exhaust, Vapor and diesel detail. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Cat-back exhaust and resonator
- ECU calibration for matched hardware
- Fuel pump or injector capacity upgrade
- Application-approved exhaust manifold or header

## Worked example

A downstream resonator makes a steady-rpm cabin tone quieter but does little to the peak exterior reading. That supports a limited acoustic claim. It supplies no evidence about emissions compliance or torque. Inventory every sensor and catalyst on the exact car before defining where a downstream modification begins.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: Two sound measurements use different road speeds and microphone locations. Which claim can be made?
step: Repeat at fixed load/rpm, microphone position and comparable background conditions.
answer: Until then report observations only; check applicable noise rules by their own prescribed method.
```

## Independent workshop

Mock up a removable cold exhaust section in card or tube off the vehicle. Locate service joints, hot-movement allowance and retained emissions interfaces; compare two acoustic designs on paper or a safe sound fixture.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Separate low-voltage diagnosis from traction work
lessons.body:
A hybrid may be ready to propel while its engine is silent. A 12 V disconnection alone does not establish that traction circuits are safe. Use vehicle-specific service and emergency information and hand high-voltage isolation or measurements to qualified personnel. Compare emissions repairs with the original approved configuration. Retain the catalyst, sensors, evaporative controls and functional diagnostics applicable to the build.

## Worked shop case

An engine is quiet but the READY indicator is on. Treat propulsion as available. For a diagnostic exercise, use the trainer outside the vehicle and select the exact model's service-information entry for a technician handoff.

## Guided practice

A drive cycle reports 5 of 7 supported monitors complete. How many supported monitors are still incomplete?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

The selected test differentiates the hypotheses and the restored state is actually measured. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Fuel supply and storage; Airflow and throttle; Ignition; Exhaust manifold and feedback; Gasoline controls; Diesel aftertreatment. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fuel supply and storage | Return / returnless; in-tank supply / additional high-pressure stage | Pressure regulation, line routing, tank venting and service access change. | Trace pressure stages, vent, purge and donor rollover provisions on the exact drawing. |
| Airflow and throttle | MAF / speed-density; mechanical / electronic throttle | Measured mass and inferred charge require different checks; throttle commands have feedback. | Compare commanded and observed data under the same conditions. |
| Ignition | Distributor / shared coil / coil-on-plug | Primary timing and secondary routing determine which cylinders can share a fault. | Use an authorized controlled swap or specified signal test to localize a trainer fault. |
| Exhaust manifold and feedback | Single / split bank; narrowband / wideband sensor | Bank identification and signal type determine how feedback is interpreted. | Mark banks, pre- and post-catalyst sensors, flex joints, hangers and shielding clearance. |
| Gasoline controls | Three-way catalyst / EGR / EVAP | These address different pollutants or vapor paths; one cannot replace another. | Map each donor device and its enable criteria and preserve the approved configuration. |
| Diesel aftertreatment | Oxidation catalyst / DPF / SCR | Oxidation, particulate capture and NOx reduction are different functions. | Identify temperature, pressure and reductant data and record the approved service route. |

references.title: Engine control, vapor and exhaust · Engine control module to Throttle pedal position sensor
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Engine control module

**Function.** Commands fueling, ignition, actuators and diagnostics.

**Design.** Match engine identity, immobilizer, harness, transmission and applicable calibration.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use a supported matched controller and retain required control and monitoring equipment.

**Verify.** Confirm software ID, communications, monitor function and fault status.

### Crankshaft position sensor and target

**Function.** Report phase reference and engine speed.

**Design.** Match trigger pattern, polarity, air gap and controller input.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Mount specified pickup on a rigid datum and index the correct target.

**Verify.** Compare waveform and index to service reference.

### Camshaft position sensor

**Function.** Identifies cam phase for sequenced operation.

**Design.** Match target, sensor type and angular relationship to crank.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install specified sensor and route away from interference.

**Verify.** Check synchronization and phase plausibility.

### Mass-airflow sensor

**Function.** Measures incoming air mass at its housing.

**Design.** Match transfer function, cross-section, flow direction and approach length.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Retain validated housing and clean, sealed flow path.

**Verify.** Log airflow versus reference under matched conditions.

### MAP sensor

**Function.** Measures absolute manifold pressure.

**Design.** Choose pressure range, port and control calibration.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit a matched sensor to a clean reference port.

**Verify.** Compare engine-off reading with local barometric reference.

### Intake-air temperature sensor

**Function.** Reports charge temperature.

**Design.** Choose location representative of measured charge and sensor curve.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use matched thermistor or integrated sensor and protect connector.

**Verify.** Compare cold-soak reading with an independent temperature reference.

### Coolant temperature sensor

**Function.** Reports coolant temperature to controls or gauge.

**Design.** Match thread, sealing method and resistance curve.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install approved sensor in the intended wetted passage.

**Verify.** Compare cold-soaked and warmed data to independent references.

### Throttle pedal position sensor

**Function.** Reports driver demand with plausibility channels.

**Design.** Match pedal module, travel, controller and correlation logic.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched pedal with stops and clear footwell.

**Verify.** Compare channels through full permitted travel.

references.title: Engine control, vapor and exhaust · Knock sensor to Muffler and resonator
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Knock sensor

**Function.** Detects block vibration used in combustion control.

**Design.** Match frequency response, block location and clamping conditions.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install specified sensor on correct clean mounting face.

**Verify.** Check circuit and permitted diagnostic data for plausibility.

### Oxygen or air-fuel sensor

**Function.** Reports exhaust oxygen for mixture control or monitoring.

**Design.** Match narrow/wideband electronics, bank position, heater and thermal limits.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved sensor and route wiring clear of exhaust heat and motion.

**Verify.** Check heater and expected signal response using exact data.

### Ignition coil

**Function.** Raises voltage to initiate spark.

**Design.** Match primary controls, dwell strategy, mounting and insulation.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched coil with intact boot and clean grounding where applicable.

**Verify.** Compare command and cylinder response using approved test equipment.

### Spark plug

**Function.** Initiates spark at the combustion chamber.

**Design.** Match thread reach, heat range, seat type, resistance and prescribed gap.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched plug on clean threads to its specified tightening procedure.

**Verify.** Record gap where adjustable and inspect firing condition.

### High-pressure fuel pump

**Function.** Raises supply pressure for direct injection or common rail.

**Design.** Match drive, rated pressure and control method to engine.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use trained, clean-system installation and exact pressure isolation and line-replacement rules.

**Verify.** Use approved pressure data and leak procedure without hand searching.

### Exhaust manifold and gasket

**Function.** Collect hot exhaust from cylinders and seal the head joint.

**Design.** Match port, thermal expansion, sensor and catalyst locations.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit compatible manifold, gasket, shielding and supports per specification.

**Verify.** Inspect leaks, sensor routing and hot clearances.

### Catalytic converter

**Function.** Converts specified pollutants in the exhaust.

**Design.** Select the lawful and approved application, position, volume and control arrangement.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install applicable replacement or retained donor unit with correct sensors and hangers.

**Verify.** Verify original control functions, leaks and applicable inspection evidence.

### Muffler and resonator

**Function.** Attenuate exhaust sound in different frequency bands.

**Design.** Choose flow capacity, internal acoustic design, space and heat clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Build supported downstream tubing around compatible silencing components.

**Verify.** Check leaks, cabin drone, applicable noise rules and clearance when hot.

references.title: Engine control, vapor and exhaust · Exhaust hanger and flex section to SCR catalyst and reductant injector
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Exhaust hanger and flex section

**Function.** Allow powertrain motion without stressing hot joints.

**Design.** Choose travel, support spacing, thermal expansion and material.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Place compliant supports on reviewed brackets with correct flex alignment.

**Verify.** Check clearance cold/hot and with expected engine movement.

### Heat shield

**Function.** Reduces radiant heat reaching body, fuel, wiring or occupants.

**Design.** Design shielding coverage, air gap, attachment and corrosion allowance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Pattern and form sheet on a bench, hem edges and isolate dissimilar materials.

**Verify.** Measure protected-side temperature at matched duty and inspect attachments.

### EGR valve and cooler

**Function.** Meter and cool recirculated exhaust where fitted.

**Design.** Match flow, controls and cooling circuit to rated donor configuration.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched clean passages and approved hardware.

**Verify.** Compare command, flow response and leakage.

### EVAP canister

**Function.** Stores fuel vapor for controlled purge.

**Design.** Match capacity, vent routing and permitted vehicle system.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved canister upright as specified with correct vapor-resistant lines.

**Verify.** Run the manufacturer's approved monitor or leak check.

### Purge and vent valves

**Function.** Connect stored vapor to intake and manage venting or leak tests.

**Design.** Match normally open/closed state, flow and connector to donor.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install identified valves on their correct ports without swapping lines.

**Verify.** Command each valve and verify expected pressure/flow response.

### Diesel oxidation catalyst

**Function.** Oxidizes selected exhaust constituents in its intended thermal range.

**Design.** Match certified engine and aftertreatment sequence.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit the correct assembly with specified sensors and insulation.

**Verify.** Check inlet/outlet data and monitor results.

### Diesel particulate filter

**Function.** Traps particulates for controlled regeneration and servicing.

**Design.** Match ash capacity, pressure sensing and engine configuration.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit specified DPF and reconnect indexed pressure tubes and temperature sensors.

**Verify.** Check pressure differential at known flow and approved service history.

### SCR catalyst and reductant injector

**Function.** Convert NOx using metered reductant.

**Design.** Match catalyst, injector, dosing control and temperature window.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched unit, lines and sensors using clean approved materials.

**Verify.** Check dosing, NOx feedback and required readiness.

### EVAP vapor line

**Function.** Carries tank vapors between tank, canister and engine.

**Design.** Use compatible low-permeation hose and routing with no unintended liquid traps.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install specified line, indexed fittings and supports away from exhaust heat.

**Verify.** Verify routing and sealing with the approved EVAP test.

### DPF differential-pressure sensor and tubes

**Function.** Measure exhaust pressure difference across the particulate filter.

**Design.** Match range, port order, heat-resistant tubes and sensor location.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit the matched sensor and route upstream/downstream tubes to correct taps.

**Verify.** Check zero/equal-pressure plausibility and readings under specified flow.

### NOx sensor and controller

**Function.** Measure exhaust NOx in the intended monitoring position.

**Design.** Match generation, upstream/downstream location, wiring and thermal limits.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit vehicle-specific sensor and follow any required initialization.

**Verify.** Check specified warm-up, diagnostics and response data.

### DEF tank and delivery pump

**Function.** Store and supply reductant to the SCR dosing system.

**Design.** Match reductant-compatible materials, heating provisions and controller.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved tank, pump and lines with scrupulous cleanliness.

**Verify.** Check commanded pressure, level and freeze-protection functions as equipped.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

writing.title: Design a two-hypothesis diagnostic test
writing.prompt: Select a gasoline sensor fault. Compare sensor bias with a wiring fault, name the evidence each predicts, and give a test that separates them. Include a diesel aftertreatment comparison and a model-specific hybrid handoff for an energized-vehicle concern. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Fuel supply and storage; Airflow and throttle; Ignition; Exhaust manifold and feedback; Gasoline controls; Diesel aftertreatment. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Separate an acoustic improvement from an emissions change
writing.prompt: Mock up a removable cold exhaust section in card or tube off the vehicle. Locate service joints, hot-movement allowance and retained emissions interfaces; compare two acoustic designs on paper or a safe sound fixture. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.

labs.title: Capture a real scan and diagnose a trainer fault
labs.intro: A scan record, a diagnosed physical trainer and a verified restoration. Plan shop time with your supervisor over the sessions the work actually takes.
safety: Use a protected low-voltage trainer for introduced faults. No emissions-control modification or traction-voltage work. Run a combustion vehicle outdoors only where authorized.
materials: Fault-capable physical OBD trainer and compatible scan tool
steps: Read and save baseline live values, units, code state and available freeze-frame/readiness data.
Ask a partner to select a hidden trainer fault. Test two hypotheses with independent evidence.
Record the identified cause, restore the trainer and compare the original variables. Explain code history or monitor states that persist.
Label any unsupported fields and document differences from a real vehicle. Identify the qualified handoff for the hybrid example.
